title: Power Automate for desktop: flowchart mode for building and viewing desktop flows
summary: The briefing accurately describes the preview designer, maker-selected mode and roadmap targets. Microsoft documentation supports the licensing background and switching prerequisite; independent searches found no feature-specific admin switch, automation operation or separate licensing charge.

claims.claim: The roadmap feature introduces flowchart authoring for desktop flows in Power Automate.
claims.quote: Flowchart mode introduces a new visual authoring experience in Power Automate for desktop that allows makers to create, view, and edit desktop flows using a flowchart representation.

Desktop flow actions appear as nodes on a canvas in flowchart mode.

claims.claim: Edges between nodes represent execution paths.
claims.quote: Each action is represented as a node, and edges connect the nodes to show their execution paths.

claims.claim: Microsoft says this view can make branches, loops and complex execution paths easier to understand.
claims.quote: This view can make execution paths easier to understand, especially in flows that contain branches, loops, or other complex logic.

claims.claim: Sequence mode remains a designer mode displaying actions as a numbered list.

claims.claim: In Power Automate for desktop, Console > New flow > Create a flow > Flowchart mode (Preview) selects the new flow's mode.
claims.quote:
In the console, select **New flow**.
In the **Create a flow** dialog, enter a name for the desktop flow. If you leave the field empty, a name is generated automatically.
Select **Flowchart mode (Preview)**.

claims.claim: An existing desktop flow can be switched to flowchart mode through View > Flowchart mode in its designer.
claims.quote:
Open the desktop flow in the designer.
Select **View**.
To open the flow in flowchart mode, select **Flowchart mode**.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: An existing desktop flow can be switched to sequence mode through View > Sequence mode in its designer.
claims.quote:
Open the desktop flow in the designer.
Select **View**.
To open the flow in sequence mode, select **Sequence mode**.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature changes how a flow is visualized and edited rather than introducing a separate runtime flow.
claims.quote:
You can change the visualization of a desktop flow without creating a separate flow.
Flowchart mode changes how you visualize and edit the current subflow.

claims.claim: Action-based conditions such as If process and If file exists retain their standard properties dialogs.
claims.quote: Action-based conditions, such as **If process** and **If file exists**, continue to use their standard properties dialogs.

claims.claim: An action added from an edge is inserted before its properties dialog opens.
claims.quote: The action is added to the flow before its properties dialog opens.

claims.claim: Closing the inserted action's properties dialog does not remove the action.
claims.quote: Closing or canceling the dialog doesn't remove the action from the flow.

claims.claim: Move changes only a node's visual position.
claims.quote: Moving a node changes only its visual position. It doesn't change the flow's execution order.

claims.claim: Reorder changes the flow's execution order.
claims.quote: Reordering changes the flow's execution order.

claims.claim: Move and Reorder have different keyboard shortcuts.
claims.quote: The Ctrl+Shift+Arrow shortcuts change only the node's position on the canvas. The Shift+Alt+Arrow shortcuts change the flow's execution order.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium provides access to premium RPA features, except unattended RPA and hosted RPA.
claims.quote: The **Power Automate Premium** license provides access to all RPA premium features, except unattended RPA and hosted RPA.

claims.claim: The premium RPA feature list does not include flowchart mode.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to flowchart mode.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Flowchart mode is user-opt-in: makers choose it while sequence mode is selected by default.
claims.quote:
Select **Flowchart mode (Preview)**.
Sequence mode is selected by default. Flowchart mode is identified as a preview feature in the **Create a flow** dialog.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for selecting the maker's flowchart or sequence designer mode.
claims.quote: Searched: flowchart mode API PowerShell pac workflow visualization; read desktop-flow-public-apis, searched the full Workflow entity reference for flowchart/visualization/designer/sequence, and read pac/PowerShell results. No mode-setting operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant, environment or registry switch allowing or blocking flowchart mode is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Power Automate desktop flowchart mode disable admin registry environment setting default mode' and flowchart Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell; read feature/governance pages, Workflow reference and CLI results. No feature switch found.

claims.claim: None of the registry settings on the desktop governance page names flowchart mode.
claims.quote: Searched: flowchart mode disable admin registry; fetched governance and searched its complete text for flowchart and all section headings. No flowchart-mode registry setting appears.

claims.claim: The governance page documents existing registry controls for sign-in.
claims.quote: Use the following registry entry to keep users from signing in to Power Automate for desktop using a Microsoft account.

claims.claim: Existing registry controls can restrict access to Power Automate for desktop as a whole rather than configuring flowchart mode specifically.
claims.quote: If all the following registry keys are set to 1, users can't sign in to Power Automate for desktop using any type of account.

claims.claim: Documentation does not describe a mode being automatically applied to existing flows without a maker's choice.
claims.quote: Searched: flowchart mode disable admin registry environment setting default mode; read flowchart-flow-designer in full, governance and desktop-flow-public-apis. No automatic conversion, runtime change or admin-side mode choice is described.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a credit rate specific to flowchart mode.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Power Automate desktop flowchart mode license pricing credits meter premium'; read the feature page, premium-features, licensing FAQ and returned licensing/pricing excerpts. No flowchart-specific credit rate found.

claims.claim: The governance page documents an existing registry control for manual updates.
claims.quote: Use the following registry entry to prevent users from manually updating Power Automate for desktop and receiving update notifications.

claims.claim: The governance page documents an existing registry control for proxy configuration.
claims.quote: IT administrators can set the following registry key to configure how Power Automate interacts with a corporate proxy server.

claims.claim: The governance page documents existing registry controls for logging.
claims.quote: Use the following registry entry to prevent Power Automate for desktop from uploading detailed logs per action for the respective run of the flow's run history, after a desktop flow execution.

claims.claim: The sources describe no change seen by runtime users or administrators.
claims.quote: Searched: flowchart mode disable admin registry environment setting default mode; read flowchart-flow-designer, governance and desktop-flow-public-apis. Sources describe a maker-selected visualization, with no runtime-user or admin-facing change.
